assessment: Pal and colleagues show that hydrogen sulfide (H2S) inhibits HIV replication and reactivation by a variety of mechanisms including inhibition of NF-κB and recruitment of the epigenetic silencer, YY1, to the HIV promoter. They further report that H2S helps in maintaining mitochondrial bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Altogether, the study provides novel insights into the mechanisms underlying HIV transcription and reactivation.
